model_result.answer_summary: PL1 is a cardiolipin assembled from 2 phosphate units (b), 3 glycerol units (c), 4 acyl residues R-CO- (d) and n = 6 H caps (a; n derived: stub parity gives n even [answer 5.1 (a)], acyclicity + connectivity give n = 6). Structure: R-COO-CH2-CH(O2CR)-CH2-O-P(=O)(OH)-O-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-O-P(=O)(OH)-O-CH2-CH(O2CR)-CH2-O-CO-R, acyclic, peroxide-free, diprotic (two identical P-OH), consistent with the Q5-4 hydrolysis PL1 + 8 H2O -> 4 RCOOH + 2 H3PO4 + 3 glycerol (exactly 8 ester bonds). One enantiomer: (R,R) at the two outer glycerol sn-2 carbons (CIP: 1 = sn-2 O-CO-R, 2 = CH2-O-P arm [reaches P, Z=15], 3 = CH2-O-CO-R arm [reaches C], 4 = H), drawn with O-CO-R dashed behind and C-H wedged in front at each stereocentre; (S,S) is the archaeal mirror image, (R,S)/(S,R) are meso (plane of symmetry). Monoanion Y (= PL1 - H+): one phosphate deprotonated (charge delocalised over P=O / P-O(-)), stabilised by an intramolecular hydrogen-bond network: the free 2-OH of the central glycerol and the remaining acidic P-OH of the second phosphate both H-bond to the anionic non-bridging phosphate oxygen (six-membered pseudo-ring O-H...O(-)-P-O-CH2-CH). The second deprotonation destroys this network, explaining pK_a2 >> pK_a1.
assumptions: Trusted general laws used: tetravalent carbon, divalent oxygen, monovalent hydrogen, pentavalent tetrahedral phosphate P(=O)(OH)(OR)(OR'), tetrahedral carbon stereochemistry with CIP priority rules, intramolecular hydrogen-bond stabilisation of conjugate bases, resonance delocalisation of phosphate negative charge over non-bridging oxygens.

Standard biochemical fact (trusted general law class): the cardiolipin enantiomer of prokaryotes and eukaryotes has the (R,R) configuration at the two outer sn-2 glycerol carbons (glycerophospholipid backbone derived from sn-glycerol-3-phosphate); the problem requests one enantiomer, so this choice is sufficient.
Derived inline from problem-only material: n = 6 (parity + acyclicity from fragment counts and problem statements of 5.1), i.e. the 5.1 dependency was not taken from any official answer.
Cross-checked against the problem-stated hydrolysis equation on Q5-4 (PL1 + 8 H2O -> 4 RCOOH + 2 H3PO4 + 3 glycerol): the proposed structure contains exactly 8 ester bonds.

The exact nature ('special, stable structure') of Y is not specified beyond the pKa separation; the two-donor intramolecular hydrogen-bond network is the standard cardiolipin explanation and is drawn explicitly; this is a chemistry-inference step grounded in the problem facts (free central 2-OH, two P-OH acidic groups, close phosphate proximity).
